candidates.name: ProcDump
verified_facts: ProcDump can monitor applications and generate dumps for CPU, exception, hang, termination, and performance-counter triggers
Dump type and trigger options must be recorded with the target PID and output path
semantic_limits: ProcDump monitoring or dump creation is diagnostic and does not prove the canonical runner completed or published receipts

candidates.name: MiniDumpWriteDump
verified_facts: MiniDumpWriteDump writes user-mode minidump information to a specified file
Process, process ID, output handle, dump type, return value, and GetLastError result are material evidence
semantic_limits: DbgHelp dump calls require synchronization and a valid dump does not prove task success

candidates.name: MINIDUMP_TYPE
verified_facts: MINIDUMP_TYPE selects which classes of process information are written to a minidump
Available flags can vary with the DbgHelp version
semantic_limits: A dump type name alone does not prove that the requested data was captured or readable

candidates.name: Windows Error Reporting
verified_facts: Windows Error Reporting supports application faults, hangs, kernel faults, and application-specific reports
WER settings and report evidence must be read without assuming automatic upload or completion
semantic_limits: WER availability does not prove a report exists for the target runner

candidates.name: WER Functions
verified_facts: The WER API exposes report creation, dump attachment, store enumeration, metadata query, and report submission functions
Read-only store inspection can be separated from report creation or submission
semantic_limits: API availability does not establish that any report belongs to the canonical task

candidates.name: WerStoreOpen
verified_facts: WerStoreOpen opens a Windows Error Reporting report store
The selected store type and returned handle must be recorded
semantic_limits: Opening a store does not prove that it contains a relevant or fresh report

candidates.name: WerStoreGetFirstReportKey
verified_facts: WerStoreGetFirstReportKey retrieves the first report key from an opened WER store
Report keys must be enumerated and freed according to the API contract
semantic_limits: The first key is not necessarily the newest or relevant report

candidates.name: WerStoreQueryReportMetadataV2
verified_facts: WerStoreQueryReportMetadataV2 retrieves metadata for a selected WER report key
The API uses a sizing pass for associated file names
semantic_limits: Metadata must be correlated to process identity, timestamps, files, and task identity

candidates.name: WER_REPORT_METADATA_V2
verified_facts: WER_REPORT_METADATA_V2 carries report metadata and associated file information
Structure size and returned file-name data must be validated before use
semantic_limits: A structurally valid metadata record can still be stale or unrelated

candidates.name: WerStoreGetReportCount
verified_facts: WerStoreGetReportCount returns the number of reports in an opened WER store
The count can bound enumeration and detect changes between snapshots
semantic_limits: A count does not identify reports or prove relevance

candidates.name: REPORT_STORE_TYPES
verified_facts: REPORT_STORE_TYPES defines the WER stores that can be opened
The selected store must be recorded to make enumeration reproducible
semantic_limits: Different stores can contain different report sets

candidates.name: WER_DUMP_TYPE
verified_facts: WER_DUMP_TYPE defines supported WER dump classes including micro, mini, heap, and triage variants
Dump class affects captured data and sensitivity
semantic_limits: A configured type does not prove a dump was generated

candidates.name: WER_FILE_TYPE
verified_facts: WER_FILE_TYPE classifies files associated with a WER report, including dump and ETL types
File type and exact path must be captured together
semantic_limits: A file classification does not prove file integrity or task relevance

candidates.name: Service Functions
verified_facts: The service control API exposes enumeration, open, configuration, status, and control functions
Recovery evidence can use read-only enumeration and query functions
semantic_limits: Service API availability does not prove a runner is service-hosted

candidates.name: OpenSCManager
verified_facts: OpenSCManager opens a connection to the service control manager database
Requested access rights and target machine/database must be recorded
semantic_limits: Opening the SCM does not prove any service state or ownership

candidates.name: OpenService
verified_facts: OpenService opens an existing service using an SCM database handle
The exact service name and requested access rights are required evidence
semantic_limits: A service handle does not prove that the service is running or owns the runner
